section: Frequently Asked Questions
subsection: 1. What is a franchise and why should I choose franchising?
---

Franchising is a business model that offers a way for aspiring entrepreneurs to start a business without taking as many risks. It involves a mutual agreement between two parties: the franchisee (the entrepreneur) and the franchisor (the established company). With this, the franchisee gets to start and grow a business using the franchisor’s brand and proven business model, giving them a significant advantage over starting an independent business.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/?utm_source=wini&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=wini_header
section: Frequently Asked Questions
subsection: 2. How should I evaluate a franchise?
---

If you’re interested in joining a franchise, you should carefully look at their investment costs, support structure, and overall brand. Investment costs include the franchise fee, start-up costs, and ongoing fees, such as royalties and other monthly fees. Support structure is important (that’s why you join a franchise!) so carefully consider how large their support staff is and what you get for the cost. Finally, determine if it’s a brand worth investing in. You’ll want to look at the franchise’s recent awards and rankings, growth potential and franchise owner testimonials to make an informed decision.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/?utm_source=wini&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=wini_header
section: Frequently Asked Questions
subsection: 3. How do I start a home inspection business?
---

To start a home inspection business, you’ll need to establish your business entity, meet all state requirements, get trained and certified in performing inspections (and licensed if required), and obtain insurance. Whether you start an independent business or join a franchise, these steps are required; however, a franchise can help you navigate all the steps to starting your home inspection business .

section: Frequently Asked Questions
subsection: 4. What are the advantages of starting a home inspection business?
---

Starting a home inspection business offers numerous advantages including huge market potential, low upfront costs (no storefront or inventory), and potential for high-profit margins. Home inspection business owners typically generate income with every inspection, and the market is not expected to slow down anytime soon. People continue to buy and sell properties, making home inspection an essential industry and offering long-term stability and growth potential for entrepreneurs.

section: Frequently Asked Questions
subsection: 6. How much does a WIN home inspector make?
---

A WIN Home Inspection franchise owner can make a generous income, with the average gross revenue standing at $269,804 in 2025 (FDD 2026), approximately five times the average earnings of home inspectors in the U.S. However, it’s important to understand that these earnings can vary depending on several factors, including the location, owner’s experience level, number of available inspection slots in the schedule, and the price charged for each inspection. Despite these variables, WIN Home Inspection franchise owners have demonstrated the potential to earn significantly more than their industry counterparts by offering the widest range of essential services to clients, helping them generate steady income year-round. Owning a WIN franchise can be a lucrative business move, providing opportunities for substantial income while offering crucial services to home buyers, sellers, homeowners, and real estate agents in their community.

section: Frequently Asked Questions
subsection: 1. What is a veteran-owned business?
---

A veteran-owned business is a business owned and operated by a veteran. These businesses are eligible for special certifications, which can open doors to government contracts, grants and additional resources designed to support veteran entrepreneurs.

subsection: 2. How to start a business as a veteran?
---

As a veteran, your military experience can help you come up with a strong business idea, put together a solid plan, find funding and handle the legal steps to get started. Fortunately, veterans have access to numerous resources, including mentorship programs, financial assistance, and veteran-specific training to guide them through the process. WIN provides its franchise owners with all of these benefits, in addition to a robust marketing support program.

subsection: 4. How can a veteran start a business?
---

Veterans can start a business by first identifying a business idea that aligns with their skills and interests, creating a robust plan, securing funding, and registering their business. They can also explore veteran-specific resources like SBA loans, grants, and mentorship programs to support their entrepreneurial journey.

section: Frequently Asked Questions
subsection: 5. How do I become a veteran-owned small business?
---

To become a veteran-owned small business, you need to ensure that most of your business is owned and controlled by a veteran. You can then apply for certifications, such as the Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) certification, through organizations like the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, which will allow you to access special opportunities and resources.

---

Owning a home inspection franchise with WIN Home Inspection can be a rewarding and profitable venture with no hidden costs. Investing in a WIN Home Inspection franchise includes the initial franchise fee, equipment cost, marketing and training costs, insurance premiums, and additional funds for various purposes. At WIN, the initial investment to own a home inspection franchise typically ranges between $41,200 and $49,800. This comprehensive range covers all the necessary expenses involved in setting up your franchise. Moreover, WIN Home Inspection proudly offers a 10% discount to Veterans and First Responders as a token of gratitude and appreciation for their service.

section: Frequently Asked Questions
subsection: 4. How much does a WIN home inspector make?
---

A WIN Home Inspection franchise owner can make a generous income, with the average gross revenue standing at $269,804 in 2025 (FDD 2026), approximately five times the average earnings of home inspectors in the U.S. However, it’s important to understand that these earnings can vary depending on several factors, including the location, owner’s experience level, number of available inspection slots in the schedule, and the price charged for each inspection. Despite these variables, WIN Home Inspection franchise owners have demonstrated the potential to earn significantly more than their industry counterparts by offering the widest range of essential services to clients, helping them generate steady income year-round. Owning a WIN franchise can be a lucrative business move, providing opportunities for substantial income while offering crucial services to home buyers, sellers, homeowners, and real estate agents in their community.

section: How to Become a Licensed Home Inspector
subsection: 
---

Home inspectors play a key role in the real estate market. They ensure houses meet quality, safety, and structural standards. As the real estate market keeps growing becoming a home inspector brings exciting chances and a bright future.

This guide will show you how to become a home inspector. Your background or experience doesn’t matter. We aim to give a clear and simple guide for anyone who wants to join this exciting job.

Let’s dive into the world of home inspection. We’ll show you how to turn your dreams into reality in five easy steps!

- 5 Essential Steps to Becoming a Home Inspector Learn How to Become a Home Inspector in Your State: Frequently Asked Questions

Let’s dive into the world of home inspection. We’ll show you how to turn your dreams into reality in five easy steps!


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/how-to-become-a-home-inspector/
section: 5 Essential Steps to Becoming a Home Inspector
subsection: Step 1: Check Your State’s Home Inspector License Rules
---

The first step involves learning about the licensing rules in your state. These rules can differ a lot so you need to know what’s required such as education, tests, and how to apply. Some states ask for specific training or hours of education before you can get a license, while others might have different rules. Begin by checking your state’s website to find out the exact requirements for where you live.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/how-to-become-a-home-inspector/
section: 5 Essential Steps to Becoming a Home Inspector
subsection: Step 2: Finish Your Required Training Course
---

After that, you’ll have to complete a training course that your state requires. This step plays a key role because it gives you the know-how and abilities you need to carry out home inspections.

Look for a training provider approved by your area’s regulators. You can find these on their state websites. Also check out groups like the American Society of Home Inspectors (ASHI) or the International Association of Certified Home Inspectors (InterNACHI).

You can take training online, in-person, or through a mix of both. Pick the option that works best with your schedule and how you like to learn.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/how-to-become-a-home-inspector/
section: 5 Essential Steps to Becoming a Home Inspector
subsection: Step 3: Pass Your State’s Home Inspection Licensing Exam (If Required)
---

In states that require a license for home inspectors, passing the state’s exam is key. This step is crucial to show you understand the job, have the skills, and are ready to start working as a home inspector.

The exam checks how well you grasp the ideas you need to know for home inspections. Start by learning about the test format and subjects it covers. You can find this info on your state’s regulatory website. Get ready with study guides, practice tests and a look at your training materials. When you feel prepared, book your exam and take it with confidence.

» Read: Tips to Help You Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE)


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/how-to-become-a-home-inspector/
section: 5 Essential Steps to Becoming a Home Inspector
subsection: Step 4: Fill Out the State Application to Get Your License
---

Once you’ve passed the licensing exam, it’s time to apply for your state license. Begin by reviewing your state’s application requirements. These include evidence of your completed pre-licensing education, your exam scores, and proof of liability insurance. Fill out the application forms with care making sure all information is correct and complete. Errors or incomplete details can cause holdups or even result in rejection, so double-check everything before you submit.

After you’ve completed your forms, you’ll need to pay the required application fees. Make sure to keep records of your payment and all supporting documents. When you have everything ready, send in your application as directed by your state’s regulatory body. They’ll review and approve your application then issue your official license. This document permits you to work as a professional home inspector in your state.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/how-to-become-a-home-inspector/
section: 5 Essential Steps to Becoming a Home Inspector
subsection: Step 5: Get Liability Insurance and Begin Inspecting!
---

Now that you’ve got your license, the final step is to secure the right insurance. This matters before you kick off your home inspection career. General Liability Insurance plays a key role. It shields you from claims of property damage or bodily injury during an inspection. This coverage makes sure you’re safe if an accident occurs on the job, like damaging a client’s property or if someone gets hurt.

Errors & Omissions (E&O) Insurance is just as vital. It guards you against claims of negligence or mistakes in your inspection reports. If a client says you missed a critical issue, E&O insurance can cover legal costs and potential settlements. This helps protect your professional standing and financial health.

» Read: Home Inspector Insurance Cost: What You Need to Know


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/how-to-become-a-home-inspector/
section: 5 Essential Steps to Becoming a Home Inspector
subsection: – Setting Up Your Business
---

After you get insurance, start setting up your business operations. Create a business plan , set your service rates, make marketing materials, and build an online presence. When everything’s ready, dive in and begin inspections with care and professionalism.

As you gain experience, keep improving your skills and stay up-to-date with industry changes. Your reputation matters for long-term success. Focus on giving great service and building ties with real estate pros. Ask clients to leave good reviews. Your reputation is one of your best assets, and putting effort into it will pay off in the long run.


---

section: Frequently Asked Questions
subsection: 1. How long does it take to become a home inspector?
---

Becoming a home inspector takes different amounts of time. This depends on the state’s licensing rules. It also depends on how long it takes to finish the required education. Other factors include when licensing exams are available and how long it takes to process license applications. Given these considerations, it can take anywhere from a few weeks to a few months or longer to become a home inspector.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/how-to-become-a-home-inspector/
section: Frequently Asked Questions
subsection: 2. How much do home inspectors make?
---

In May 2023, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that construction and building inspectors made about $67,700 a year. This group also includes home inspectors. The income of home inspectors can vary a lot. This depends on factors like where they work, their experience level, and how many inspections they do. It also depends on the fees they charge and if they own their business.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/how-to-become-a-home-inspector/
section: Frequently Asked Questions
subsection: 3. How much does it cost to become a home inspector?
---

On average, the startup cost to become a home inspector ranges from $27,000 to $60,000. However, this cost can vary a lot. It depends on state requirements, the educational program chosen, exam fees, startup costs and insurance premiums. These costs may seem high, but this investment can lead to a rewarding and profitable career in home inspection.

section: How to Start a Home Inspection Business?

For many people, entrepreneurship has been the most reliable way to achieve financial independence and career satisfaction. Starting a home inspection business is one option.

According to a report by EMR , the United States real estate market was valued at $3.53 trillion in 2025. It is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 2.8% from 2024 to 2035, reaching a value of $4.65 trillion by 2035. About 95% of home sales involve a home inspection before closing. This positive trend reinforces the resilience of the home inspection sector. So, if you’re considering starting a home inspection business, be ready to ride a growth wave.

Starting a home inspection business has several advantages. These include steady growth, low costs, high profits, the ability to work remotely, and personal satisfaction. It’s a great industry with lots of chances to grow a high-revenue business, make connections, and serve your community.

section: What is a Home Inspection Business?
subsection: 
---

A home inspection business provides essential health and safety inspections for home buyers and sellers during real estate transactions. Appraisers consider home inspection reports when evaluating a property’s value, and insurance companies may require home inspections before granting the buyer home insurance. As a home inspector, your top priority is to help your client make an informed decision about the property they are interested in purchasing.

Buying or selling a home is a significant investment of time, energy, emotions, and financial resources, and being a trusted partner for home buyers and sellers is one of the most rewarding aspects of owning a home inspection business. You also have a responsibility to identify potential home health hazards to keep your clients informed and aware of any possible repairs they need to make. This safeguards your community and helps minimize potential financial pitfalls down the road.

section: Why You Should Start a Home Inspection Business
subsection: 
---

Rising real estate values and steady new construction continue to fuel demand for qualified home inspectors. Starting a home inspection business now enables you to enter a growing and resilient industry, positioning yourself for consistent opportunities as housing activity evolves over the coming years.

- Home inspectors are in demand: Nearly 95% of home sales include a professional inspection before closing, making inspections a standard part of the buying process. With the U.S. real estate market projected to continue growing through 2034, demand for qualified inspectors remains strong.
- Get started quickly: Even if you don’t have a background in the building trades, you can complete your training to become a home inspector in a matter of months.
- Work from home: While you will need to travel to the homes that you inspect, much of your work can be done remotely.
- It’s a transitional career: If you are a contractor or building trade professional and are thinking of a career switch, home inspection is a great way to put your knowledge and skills to use in your own business!

section: How to Start a Home Inspection Business in 10 Simple Steps
subsection: Step 1: Create a Home Inspection Business Plan
---

Every successful business venture begins with a plan, helping you make decisions about how and when to start your business. You can start your business as an independent or join a franchise .

Start by conducting a SWOT analysis, identifying the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats for your business. This will help you understand the market landscape and growth opportunities. Then, determine your target market, pricing strategy, financial projections, and operational plan.

Every aspect of the plan is essential for your business’s success. When deciding whether to start an independent business or join a franchise system, keep in mind that joining a franchise offers many benefits you can use to set yourself up for success from the beginning.

section: How to Start a Home Inspection Business in 10 Simple Steps
subsection: How to Create a Home Inspection Business Plan:
---

And stick with it! Your business name is your brand. Changing your brand after launch confuses clients and prospects, making it difficult to get an edge in your market.

Catering to all markets and demographics is impossible. In home inspection, your market consists of home buyers and sellers. At the beginning, it might be more beneficial to focus more on the buyer market to spread brand awareness.

Setting your price point is essential. Not only does it determine your income and cash flow, but it also helps you focus on your target market. If you live in an affluent area or a booming new-construction neighborhood, starting with a higher price point might be a better way to maintain steady profit margins. Conduct a competitive analysis to see where your area’s market stands with pricing.

Lay out financial goals for your business before selling your services. Think about where you’d like to take this investment in 10-15 years, and don’t let smaller roadblocks stand in the way of that.

section: How to Start a Home Inspection Business in 10 Simple Steps
subsection: Step 2: Receive Home Inspection Training
---

Home inspection is a great business opportunity for new entrepreneurs because no prior knowledge or experience is required to get started. You will, however, have to get home inspection training . This is true even if you have a background in the building trades. Home inspection is its own profession, so you’ll have to learn how to inspect homes and write up reports that meet industry standards.

Depending on where you plan to start your business, you may have a choice between classroom-based and online training programs. Training typically covers different aspects of home inspection, such as structural components, exterior and interior systems, electrical and plumbing systems, and HVAC systems. The amount of training you’ll need to get certified depends on the state where you’ll be conducting the inspections. It’s important to research the specific training requirements needed to start your home inspection business.

While most franchises will refer you to an outside training school, WIN Home Inspection includes an in-house training program at no additional cost, so you can get trained in a timely and cost-effective manner.

section: How to Start a Home Inspection Business in 10 Simple Steps
subsection: Step 3: Get Licensed and Obtain Business Insurance
---

After training, you’ll need to get certified and licensed if your state requires it. National associations like the American Society of Home Inspectors (ASHI) and the International Association of Certified Home Inspectors (InterNACHI) offer certification programs. The licensing process varies by state, with some requiring passing a state examination or completing a specific number of inspections under supervision. Once completed, you’ll receive a state license number and can begin performing home inspections for clients.

In addition to licensing, you’ll need to secure all necessary permits and purchase business insurance before you start running your business. Depending on the laws in your area and the nature of your business, such as if you’re operating out of your home, you might need certain permits or licenses as well.

Moreover, insurance plays a critical role in protecting your business. Obtain a general liability insurance policy to protect your business from potential lawsuits or claims resulting from inspections. Additionally, consider errors and omissions (E&O) insurance to cover you if a client claims you missed something during an inspection.

section: How to Start a Home Inspection Business in 10 Simple Steps
subsection: Step 4: Set Up a Legal Entity
---

Setting up a Limited Liability Company (LLC) or an S-Corp is an essential step when starting a home inspection business . An LLC protects your personal assets from being used to cover business-related debts or lawsuits. Each state has different rules for setting up an LLC, so research your state’s specific requirements or seek advice from an attorney or accountant. Even if you join a franchise, establishing an LLC or an S-Corp is still an important step in starting your home inspection business.

Here are some common terms you should familiarize yourself with:

- Sole proprietorship: A non-registered, unincorporated business run by an individual who possesses both business and owner titles.
- Partnership : An arrangement between two or more individuals to oversee a business’s operations and share its profits.
- Limited liability company (LLC): A business structure that offers protection and pass-through taxation. Limited liability allows a corporation to separate the entity from its owners, thereby making it so that owners are not legally liable for business debts, for instance.
- Corporation: A corporation is a group of people allowed to act as one single entity, facing legal consequences as one individual, as opposed to individual responsibilities.

There are many ways you can obtain a competitive edge in your market:

- Offer Multiple or Additional Services: Service variety caters to a broader number of consumers within the same market. Extend your service offerings as much as possible to account for all potential household issues.
- Provide High-Quality Service to Customers: We all know that good customer service makes for a loyal client. Being highly trained, knowledgeable, and personable, you can deliver top-notch service to your community and build a sustainable client base.
- Use Innovative and State-of-the-Art Tools: Outdated technology slows down reporting and can lead to inaccuracies. Consumers favor businesses that adopt up-to-date tools and technologies.
- Use Advanced Report Writing Software: The writing of the home inspection report must align with the appropriate insurance legalese, yet also be digestible information for home buyers and sellers. Using innovative and intuitive report-writing software helps you accomplish just that.

---

While there is no inventory required for starting a home inspection business, having the right tools and equipment is essential for providing high-quality services. Your home inspector toolkit should include items like a drone, a moisture meter, electrical testers, gas leak detectors, thermal imaging devices, and more. You may also need equipment, including ladders, stepstools, toolboxes and belts, and safety equipment.

When investing in tools, prioritize accuracy, safety, and reliability over flashy extras. Start with the essentials required in your state and by your insurance provider, then upgrade as your business grows to expand service offerings and increase inspection value for clients.

subsection: Step 10: Be Patient
---

Building a successful home inspection business doesn’t happen overnight; it’s a journey that requires persistence, resilience, and time. It can take months, sometimes years, to establish a solid client base and achieve consistent profitability. During this period, it’s important not to get disheartened by initial challenges or slower-than-expected growth.

Instead, see these as learning opportunities that will eventually lead to better business strategies. Remember, every successful business today was once a start-up navigating through uncertainties.

section: What Does a Home Inspector Do Day-to-Day?
subsection: 
---

As a home inspector, you’re professionally trained and certified to detect the true condition of a residential property. Pre-listing inspections can improve home buyers’ confidence before they complete a transaction.

Essentially, as a home inspector, you could be squeezing through a crawlspace to inspect insulation issues, and the next moment you’re scaling ladders for roof work.

Your job carries significant responsibilities, which may include:

- Inspecting various property elements like roofing, plumbing, and a building’s overall structural integrity. Site inspections may also include verifying safety features such as fire extinguisher placements and smoke detection systems.
- Generating and explaining site assessment reports. These give home buyers peace of mind by ensuring that the property meets their expectations.
- Clearly communicating with clients to identify every concern.
- Offering specialized health and environmental services like mold testing and infrared scans. These add-on specializations can boost revenue and are not part of standard home inspection training.

section: What Is the Trade Service Industry? A Complete Guide
subsection: 
---

When someone is building a home, they hire a slew of skilled workers, ranging from framers and plumbers to engineers and general contractors, and everyone in between. In the same way, when it’s time to fix their car, they go to a licensed mechanic, a hair stylist when it’s time for a cut, and the list goes on.

These individuals and companies offer specialized, hands-on skills and knowledge to provide key services, and demand for these services continues to rise.

High-demand sectors, particularly construction and maintenance, need new workers. Why? Because on-site, hands-on, specialized expertise cannot be easily automated or outsourced.

Interested in entering the trade service industry, specifically the home services sector? Here’s what you need to know and how to get started.

- What Is the Trade Service Industry? Types of Services in the Home Services Sector Why Demand Remains Consistent for These Businesses Why These Home-Based Trade Services Are Ideal for Franchising


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/what-is-the-trade-service-industry/
section: What Is the Trade Service Industry?
subsection: 
---

It’s well known that demand in the skilled trade service industry is on the rise.

But what are trade services?

Trade services are careers that require specialized, hands-on skills acquired through technical education, training, and apprenticeship programs. Some of the best trade jobs are in sectors like construction, maintenance, and repair, and they often require certification or licensing.

The trade service industry includes a range of skilled careers focused on providing direct services to the public, consumers, or businesses.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/what-is-the-trade-service-industry/
section: What Is the Trade Service Industry?
subsection: Why the Trade Service Industry Matters
---

Given the services it provides, the trade services industry remains foundational to the modern economy. When looking at the numbers, the impact of these careers is apparent, as is the opportunity ahead.

According to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, projections indicate a 4% to 60% growth in skilled trades through 2033, depending on the specific role. This projected growth is driven by an aging workforce and ongoing infrastructure investments. This high demand for skilled labor has led to competitive salaries and high job satisfaction. Many of the roles also offer alternatives to traditional jobs that require four-year degrees.

This growth is creating a domino effect, with careers related to core skilled trades. For example, the real estate market and home inspection industry are tied to skill trades. This interdependence underscores that a strong economy requires support for both the skilled trades and the professional services that enable them.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/what-is-the-trade-service-industry/
section: Types of Services in the Home Services Sector
subsection: 
---

The home services sector covers a range of specialized services focused on repairing, maintaining, improving, and cleaning residential properties. These services are crucial for property upkeep and increasingly in demand, particularly when aiming for greater safety and efficiency .


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/what-is-the-trade-service-industry/
section: Types of Services in the Home Services Sector
subsection: Home Repair and Maintenance Services
---

Home repair and maintenance services focus on a property’s functionality and value. The goal is typically to preserve a property’s value, ensure safety, enhance efficiency, and extend the lifespan of home systems. In many cases, service providers are called in when something breaks or a small issue arises, so it doesn’t turn into a costly emergency.

Examples include maintenance services that address general repairs, painting, and fixture installations. There are also skilled trades services for repair-based scenarios that overlap with construction-related trades, ranging from roofing to HVAC installation and repair. There are also some highly specialized services, such as window or carpet cleaning.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/what-is-the-trade-service-industry/
section: Types of Services in the Home Services Sector
subsection: Construction-Related Trades
---

As discussed, construction-related tradespeople are needed for repair and maintenance scenarios, but they are also called in for new builds.

HVAC professionals, plumbers, electricians, carpenters, roofers, drywallers, and masons are all skilled trades. These service providers often require certification, licensing, and apprenticeships, commonly operating as subcontractors under general contractors.

While some specialize in new construction , others offer guidance for various phases of homeownership. For example, a roofing company may be called after an inspection to address water damage or other roof-related repairs .


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/what-is-the-trade-service-industry/
section: Types of Services in the Home Services Sector
subsection: Specialized Services
---

Specialized services are those that help solve urgent problems or enhance a home’s security or aesthetics. Examples include landscaping services, chimney cleaning, pest control, garage door installation services, security system upgrades, etc.

A specialized service that overlaps with all of the above home services is home inspections. A qualified home inspector provides a comprehensive visual assessment of a property’s systems. This assessment includes structural integrity, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and exterior components to identify defects, safety hazards, and necessary repairs. These services may be requested by the home seller or home buyer.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/what-is-the-trade-service-industry/
section: Why Demand Remains Consistent for These Businesses
subsection: 
---

Skilled trades businesses remain in high demand because they are foundational to modern infrastructure, emergency maintenance services, energy efficiency, and more. In many cases, these businesses provide services that cannot be delayed or ignored. However, many trade jobs also focus on a proactive vs. reactive approach.

For example, following a full home inspection or roof inspection , a leak in attic flashing may be discovered. A homeowner would want to address that immediately to prevent costly roof repairs later, including replacing ceiling joists and insulation. So, trade service businesses address both. They provide proactive services, focusing on prevention, routine, and long-term planning, as well as reactive services, focusing on repairs and urgency. Both provide steady work.

There is also consistent work due to the nature of the job, which involves trade services and is subject to mandatory regulations. Building codes and safety regulations require licensed technicians for inspections, installations, repairs, and upgrades.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/what-is-the-trade-service-industry/
section: Why Demand Remains Consistent for These Businesses
subsection: How These Businesses Operate
---

As essential, high-demand, and specialized businesses, trade service providers may operate under a service-based model. This model often provides labor-intensive on-site services, generating revenue through hourly rates, job-based flat fees, or maintenance contracts.

To provide these services, companies must offer clients licensed, certified professionals. For many, this is their unique selling point, helping them limit competition. As they build their portfolios and reputation, most focus on their local area, building a local reputation based on trust and reliability. Clients will often prioritize speed, expertise, and reliability over cost, especially in emergency situations.

section: Can You Make 6 Figures as a Home Inspector?
subsection: 
---

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, the average salary of a building inspector is $72,120 a year. But that’s just the average. Many entrepreneurs build successful inspection businesses that gross more than $100,000. This level of home inspector earnings takes time and work, but there are steps you can take after passing the exam and getting your state license to stay headed in the right direction.

A six-figure income depends on the number of inspections you schedule, how much you plan on charging, where you live, your level of experience, and your ability to market yourself and find work year-round. This guide breaks down the math, the challenges you face, and the actual path to building a six-figure home inspection business.

- How to Reach Your Six-Figure Target: The Basics Key Factors to Increase Your Income Home Inspector Pay vs. Home Inspector Business Owner Earnings Operating Costs Accelerating Your Business Growth With a Franchise


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/can-you-make-6-figures-as-a-home-inspector/
section: How to Reach Your Six-Figure Target: The Basics
subsection: 
---

To consistently earn a six-figure income as a home inspector, start by setting clear goals. Determine how many jobs you need annually by dividing your target salary by your average inspection fee. For example, if your business operates in an area where homes sell for $300,000 to $450,000, you might charge an average fee of $500 for a standard home inspection. To make an annual gross income of $100,000 at $500 per job, you’ll need to complete at least 200 home inspections throughout the year. Assuming you work 50 weeks a year and take two weeks of vacation, that breaks down to a manageable target of just four inspections per week.

If the homes in your area sell for less, you’ll have to increase your target number of inspections. On the other hand, if you live in a major city, like Seattle, where the inspection fees for a 2,500 square foot home are around $645, you might need only 155 inspections per year to reach your goal, thus reducing your weekly target to three inspections per week.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/can-you-make-6-figures-as-a-home-inspector/
section: Key Factors to Increase Your Income
subsection: 
---

A good estimate of how much work you’ll need is only the first step in reaching your financial goals. Other factors include location, experience, pricing, and the effort you put into growing your business.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/can-you-make-6-figures-as-a-home-inspector/
section: Key Factors to Increase Your Income
subsection: 1. Location and Market Size
---

The current real estate market will determine how much people will pay for your services. If you live in an area with a lot of growth that sees thousands of real estate transactions each year, you’ll be more successful at finding new clients than you would in a small town where not a lot of people move in and out.

Before you get started, research recent and historical home sales in your local market. Subscribe to the MLS ( multiple listing service ) of your choice, and examine local market statistics. Get familiar with the information offered on various websites, including NAR , Zillow , and Realtor.com . Most real estate brokerages also offer in-depth information, and you can download local housing market info from Redfin.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/can-you-make-6-figures-as-a-home-inspector/
section: Key Factors to Increase Your Income
subsection: 2. Pricing Strategy and Additional Services
---

The average home inspection cost for a small home is between $250 and $400. In high-priced markets, the cost can reach $1,000 or more for a large home, condo, or rental in a desirable, big-city neighborhood. Some home inspectors may also charge by the size of the home, with the average ranging from $0.15 to $0.30 per square foot.

Home inspectors also know that by offering additional services, they can increase the total profit per appointment, depending on what’s needed and what the client requests.

Ancillary inspection services include radon testing, indoor air quality checks, sewer camera inspections, termite inspections, and more. By offering multiple services, you help potential home buyers, sellers, and homeowners solve more problems.

A basic $400 home inspection quickly turns into an $800 invoice when you add a sewer scope and a multi-day radon test. If these services are typically needed in your area, you’ll be able to reduce the number of inspections needed to meet your annual goals. For example, the EPA recommends radon testing in all homes at least every two years, which can add $100-$200 to the final cost.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/can-you-make-6-figures-as-a-home-inspector/
section: Key Factors to Increase Your Income
subsection: 3. Gaining Experience
---

In the beginning, time will be your biggest challenge. As a new inspector, it may take you three to four hours to complete an on-site inspection. As you gain knowledge and experience, you’ll develop efficient habits and reduce the time you spend. An experienced inspector can complete home inspections faster than someone just starting out, making it easier to schedule and complete more inspections each day.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/can-you-make-6-figures-as-a-home-inspector/
section: Key Factors to Increase Your Income
subsection: 4. Understanding Seasonal Changes
---

The real estate market fluctuates throughout the year. Typically, there are more sales in spring and summer than in winter and fall. To maintain a six-figure income, you’ll need to build your business so it survives the drop in sales in the cooler months.

The best way to build your business is through real estate agent referrals. Agents prefer to work with inspectors who arrive on time, communicate clearly, and provide detailed, professional reports. Establish relationships with as many agents in the area as you can to ensure that when the winter market slows down, the few agents who are still closing deals will look to you as their first choice for inspections.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/can-you-make-6-figures-as-a-home-inspector/
section: Home Inspector Pay vs. Home Inspector Business Owner Earnings
subsection: 
---

There’s a big difference in income between working for a home inspection company and running your own home inspection business. When you work for someone else, they find the clients to keep you busy year-round. That means less busy-work for you, but they also take a cut of the money you make with inspections. The amount varies depending on how well-established the company you work for is.

As a home inspector business owner, you’ll keep 100% of your profits after taxes and business expenses. Additionally, as you grow your company and start hiring workers to help you, you also get to keep a portion of the money they make. Most entrepreneurs start as sole proprietors and build up their client base until they reach six figures.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/can-you-make-6-figures-as-a-home-inspector/
section: Operating Costs
subsection: 
---

It’s important to factor in operating costs when determining your overall profit. As a business owner, you’ll need to purchase Errors and Omissions Insurance and general liability insurance to protect yourself if you miss a hidden defect in the property and any damage occurs while you’re inspecting. You must also purchase professional tools, like thermal imaging cameras, moisture meters, and inspection reporting software. You’ll also be responsible for your own taxes and private insurance.

When estimating how many inspections you need to earn $100,000 annually, be sure to deduct all monthly and yearly expenses, as well as federal and state taxes. You’ll need to adjust accordingly.


---
source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/can-you-make-6-figures-as-a-home-inspector/
section: Accelerating Your Business Growth With a Franchise
subsection: 
---

Building a business from scratch takes a lot of persistence, hard work, and time. As a new business owner, you’ll likely spend the first several years making mistakes, testing different marketing ideas, and trying to figure out the smartest way to operate. The best way to skip this trial-and-error phase is by joining a reputable franchise organization.

By partnering with a well-known brand like WIN Home Inspection , you can start making more money right after opening your doors. Instead of starting with a blank slate, a franchise has already completed all the hard work for you. You’ll get a complete, ready-to-use system from day one.

Organizations like WIN Home Inspection provide structured training programs. This training gives you access to professional marketing materials and the credibility of a nationally recognized brand name. From the very first day you walk into a real estate office, agents will trust you much more than if you’re an unknown startup.

By using established systems and marketing plans, you set yourself up for a more predictable flow of business, which helps you achieve a six-figure income much faster. For more information on successful franchise development, schedule a free consultation today.

The requirements to become a home inspector, including education and examination, vary by state. Here is what to consider if you want to become an inspector in Alabama.

source: website
url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/how-to-become-a-home-inspector/alabama/
section: 6 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Alabama
subsection: 
---

1 Complete the Required Education Program 2 Complete Required Field Inspections 3 Pass the Required Exams 4 Obtain Proof of Insurance 5 Show Proof of Membership or Certification 6 Apply for Your License

1 Complete the Required Education Program Home inspector training must be approved by the Alabama Home Inspectors / EIFS Inspectors Licensing Division. A total of 120 hours of education is required to qualify for the Home Inspector License. 2 Complete Required Field Inspections You must either: Conduct 35 home inspections under the supervision of a licensed Alabama home inspector, or Complete 35 hours of approved home inspection education and participate in 100 home inspections. 3 Pass the Required Exams In Alabama, you must pass both the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) and the ASHI (American Society of Home Inspectors) Ethics Exam. The NHIE consists of 200 multiple-choice questions across three domains and has a time limit of four hours. Each attempt costs approximately $225. Taking a prep course is recommended to improve your chances of passing on the first attempt. The ASHI Ethics Exam tests your knowledge of the Standards of Practice and Code of Ethics of ASHI. 4 Obtain Proof of Insurance Home inspectors in Alabama must have Errors and Omissions (E&O) insurance with a minimum coverage of $250,000, as well as liability insurance covering $20,000 for property damage, $50,000 for personal injury or death of one person, and $100,000 for injury or death of multiple individuals. 5 Show Proof of Membership or Certification You must meet one of the following criteria: Be a member of an approved Alabama home inspection organization such as ASHI, HIF, InterNACHI, or NIBI, or Be certified by the U.S. Veterans Administration, HUD, Southern Building Code Congress International, or Council of American Building Officials, or Have a GED or high school diploma and at least 1 year of home inspection experience (100 minimum inspections). 6 Apply for Your License Once all steps are completed, you can apply for the Alabama Home Inspector License. The application must be notarized, and a fee of $300 is required. Applications can be submitted online for convenience.

section: 8 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Arizona
subsection: 
---

1 Complete Required Education 2 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) 3 Complete Parallel Inspections 4 Obtain a Fingerprint Clearance Card 5 Obtain Insurance or a Bond 6 Submit the Statement of Citizenship 7 Disclose Any Disciplinary Actions or Convictions 8 Submit Your Application and Pay the Fee

1 Complete Required Education Successfully complete 84 hours of Arizona-approved home inspection education, which aligns with the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE). 2 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) The NHIE is a 4-hour exam consisting of 200 multiple-choice questions covering property and building inspection, analysis of findings, reporting, and professional responsibilities. Taking an exam prep course is recommended to improve your chances of passing on the first attempt. Note: Veterans can get reimbursed for the exam through the GI Bill by submitting the VBA-22-0803-ARE form and their receipt to the VA. 3 Complete Parallel Inspections Conduct 30 parallel inspections, each documented in a log. Every inspection must have a notarized affidavit signed by the parallel inspector. 4 Obtain a Fingerprint Clearance Card Apply for an active fingerprint clearance card from the Arizona Department of Public Safety, which is a requirement for licensure. 5 Obtain Insurance or a Bond Arizona requires home inspectors to carry errors and omissions (E&O) insurance with a minimum coverage of $200,000 in aggregate and $100,000 per occurrence, or secure a bond of $25,000. Provide policy details and coverage dates. 6 Submit the Statement of Citizenship Complete the Arizona Statement of Citizenship and Alien Status for Public Benefits form, along with a copy of your government-issued photo ID. 7 Disclose Any Disciplinary Actions or Convictions If applicable, disclose disciplinary actions or criminal convictions related to licenses or registrations. Provide copies of the order and a detailed written explanation for any offenses. 8 Submit Your Application and Pay the Fee Pay the $175 application fee and submit your application to become a licensed home inspector in Arizona.

The fee is $250 for applications received between January 1st and June 31st. For those received between July 1st and December 1st, the fee is $375, covering the remainder of the year and the following year.

Who regulates home inspectors in California? California home inspectors are regulated under the 1996 California Trade Practice Act, which prohibits unethical home inspection practices.

section: 5 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Connecticut
subsection: 
---

1 Obtain a Home Inspector Intern Permit 2 Complete 100 Inspections Under Supervision 3 Pass the National Home Inspectors Exam 4 Acquire Proof of Insurance 5 Send the Application

1 Obtain a Home Inspector Intern Permit The intern permit is required to pursue full-on licensure. 2 Complete 100 Inspections Under Supervision Successful applicants must have completed at least one hundred home inspections under their supervisor’s watch. During the at least ten inspections, the supervisor must be physically present, and then merely available for consultation and indirect supervision during the remaining training period. The applicant must also submit logs of their inspections, signed by the supervisor. 3 Pass the National Home Inspectors Exam The NHIE consists of 200 multiple-choice questions across three domains and has a time limit of four hours. Each attempt costs approximately $225. Taking a prep course is recommended to improve your chances of passing on the first attempt. 4 Acquire Proof of Insurance While Connecticut doesn’t require insurance for home inspectors, most—including every WIN Strategic Partner—carry it. To meet the standards of many boards and homeowner associations, it’s recommended to have $100,000 in Errors and Omissions coverage and $100,000 in General Liability coverage. Additionally, ensure that your personal name is included on the insurance documents. 5 Send the Application Finally, the candidate needs to mail their application, either digitally or physically, to the DCP. They must get the application document notarized and include a payment of $290 ($250 license fee plus the $40 application fee).

section: 6 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Delaware
subsection: 
---

1 Complete 140 Hours of Approved Education 2 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam 3 Register as a Home Inspector Trainee 4 Complete 75 Supervised Home Inspections 5 Obtain Insurance 6 Apply for Licensing

1 Complete 140 Hours of Approved Education Complete 140 hours of Delaware-approved home inspection education. This training aligns with the topics covered in the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) and is essential for building a strong foundation in the industry. 2 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) After completing the required education, the next step is to register for and pass the NHIE. The exam includes 200 multiple-choice questions, with 25 questions not counted toward the final score. The exam costs approximately $225, and taking an Exam Prep course is highly recommended. 3 Register as a Home Inspector Trainee Before applying for a full Home Inspector License, you must first register as a home inspector trainee and begin supervised inspections. 4 Complete 75 Supervised Home Inspections Conduct a minimum of 75 home inspections under the active supervision of a licensed Delaware home inspector. Both you and your supervising inspector must maintain a log of these inspections, which will be submitted with your license application. 5 Obtain Insurance Delaware requires you to have general liability insurance with a minimum coverage of $250,000 and Errors and Omissions (E&O) insurance with coverage of at least $50,000. 6 Apply for a Home Inspector License and Business License To apply for your Home Inspector License, use Delaware’s DELPROS online portal. Be sure to submit all required documents, including proof of insurance and notarized forms. Additionally, you must apply for a Delaware Business License. Note: If you have prior convictions or pending charges, you will need to submit a background check as part of the application process.

section: 6 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Florida
subsection: 
---

1 Complete an Approved Training Program 2 Pass a Department-Approved Exam 3 Submit to a Background Check 4 Obtain Insurance 5 Submit Your Application and Pay Fees 6 Complete Your Education

1 Complete an Approved 120-Hour Home Inspection Training Program Applicants must successfully complete a Department-approved course of study that covers the eight components of a home. Proof of course completion must be submitted with your application. 2 Pass a Department-Approved Home Inspection Exam Applicants are required to pass one of the approved exams, such as the NHIE or FABI exam. The NHIE, for instance, consists of 200 multiple-choice questions across three domains and has a time limit of four hours. Each attempt costs approximately $225. Taking a prep course is recommended to improve your chances of passing on the first attempt. 3 Submit to a Background Check A background check is required for licensing. Submit fingerprints via a Livescan Service Provider registered with the Florida Department of Law Enforcement (FDLE) immediately after submitting your application. Processing may take up to five days. 4 Obtain Insurance Applicants must carry commercial general liability insurance with coverage of at least $300,000. Proof of insurance must be included with the application. 5 Submit Your Application and Pay Fees Submit your application to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation. The $125 application fee can be paid online via credit card or e-check, or by mail with a check payable to the Department. Military veterans, their spouses, and Florida National Guard members may be eligible for fee waivers or discounts. 6 Enroll and Complete the Required Education Program Home inspector training must be approved by the Texas Real Estate Commission (TREC). To obtain the Real Estate Inspector license, 154 hours of education (including 40 hours of practicum) are required, and to obtain the Professional Real Estate Inspector license, 194 hours of education are required (including 40 hours of practicum).

section: 4 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Illinois
subsection: 
---

1 Fulfill Education Requirements 2 Perform 5 Mock Home Inspections 3 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam 4 Submit Your Application and Pay the $250 Fee

1 Complete 60 Hours of Illinois-Approved Education The Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation requires applicants to complete a 60-hour home inspection course from an approved provider. 2 Perform 5 Mock Home Inspections As part of the education requirement, you must successfully perform and document five mock home inspections under the supervision of a licensed inspector. 3 Take and Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) The NHIE consists of 200 multiple-choice questions covering topics such as property inspection, analysis of findings, and professional responsibilities. The exam costs $225 and requires a score of 500 or higher to pass. You can schedule your exam through PSI, the designated testing provider. 4 Submit Your Application and Pay the $250 Fee Once you’ve passed the exam, submit your application to the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation. The application form can be found online, and there is a $250 application fee. Send your completed application to: IDFPR – Division of Real Estate Real Estate Education Section 320 West Washington Street, 3rd Floor Springfield, IL 62786

url_or_path: https://wini.com/franchise/how-to-become-a-home-inspector/kentucky/
section: 6 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Kentucky
subsection: 
---

1 Complete 64 Hours of Approved Education 2 Conduct 3 Unpaid Field Inspections 3 Take and Pass the NHIE 4 Submit Background Checks 5 Obtain General Liability Insurance 6 Apply for a License and Pay the $250 Fee

1 Complete 64 Hours of Approved Education Kentucky requires home inspectors to complete 64 hours of education, including 16 hours of lab-based work and practice inspections. Training must be conducted in-person, as the state does not allow online courses. 2 Conduct 3 Unpaid Field Inspections During your training, you will complete 3 unpaid inspections under the supervision of a licensed inspector. 3 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) Once your education is complete, you must pass the NHIE, a comprehensive exam consisting of 200 multiple-choice questions. Test-takers need a score of 500 or higher to pass. The exam fee is $225, and there is a 30-day waiting period between retakes. Note: Veterans may qualify for reimbursement of the NHIE exam fee under the GI Bill. To utilize this benefit, submit the VBA-22-0803-ARE form along with your exam receipt to the VA. 4 Submit Background Checks As part of the application process, you must undergo a background check from both the Kentucky State Police and the F.B.I., as well as provide fingerprints. 5 Obtain General Liability Insurance You must secure general liability insurance with a minimum coverage of $250,000. The Kentucky Board of Home Inspectors must be listed as the certificate holder on your insurance policy. 6 Apply for a License and Pay the $250 Fee Submit your completed application to the Kentucky Board of Home Inspectors, along with a non-refundable $250 fee.

section: 7 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Louisiana
subsection: 
---

1 Submit to a Criminal Background Check 2 Complete Pre-Licensing Education 3 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam 4 Complete Pre-Licensing Platform Training 5 Attend a Report Writing Seminar 6 Obtain Insurance 7 Submit Your Application to LSBHI

1 Submit to a Criminal Background Check Apply to the Louisiana State Police for a criminal background check and pay all associated costs. Submit the results to the Louisiana State Board of Home Inspectors (LSBHI). If you have concerns about your background check results, contact LSBHI before beginning any education program. 2 Complete Pre-Licensing Education Complete a minimum of 90 hours of education from an LSBHI-approved provider, which must be completed within 180 days. 3 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam The NHIE consists of 200 multiple-choice questions across three domains and has a time limit of four hours. Each attempt costs approximately $225. Taking a prep course is recommended to improve your chances of passing on the first attempt. 4 Complete Additional Platform Training and Inspections After passing the NHIE, you are required to complete 30 hours of pre-licensing platform training and participate in at least 10 live inspections under an approved in-field trainer. 5 Attend a Report Writing Seminar Attend a report writing seminar provided by an LSBHI-approved provider to enhance your reporting skills. 6 Obtain Insurance Louisiana home inspectors must carry at least $300,000 in Errors and Omissions coverage and $300,000 in General Liability coverage, with maximum deductibles of $5,000. 7 Submit Your Application to LSBHI Once all licensing requirements are met, submit your application to the LSBHI . This must be completed within 36 months of starting the licensing process.

section: 5 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Maine
subsection: 
---

1 Enroll in State-Recognized Courses 2 Take and Pass the NHIE 3 Join Professional Associations in Maine 4 Secure Relevant Insurances 5 Start Your Business or Join a Franchise

1 Enroll in State-Recognized Home Inspection Courses Although Maine does not require licensing for home inspectors, professional training is vital for understanding legal inspection standards and business practices. Enrolling in courses offered by a reputable home inspection school equips you with essential knowledge and skills to establish credibility and succeed in the industry. This training is highly valued by real estate agents, employers, and clients. By completing recommended coursework, you will be prepared for challenges in the field and for optional certification exams, like the NHIE. 2 Take and Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) The NHIE consists of 200 multiple-choice questions across three domains and has a time limit of four hours. Each attempt costs approximately $225. Taking a prep course is recommended to improve your chances of passing on the first attempt. Note: Veterans can have exam costs reimbursed through the GI Bill by submitting a VBA-22-0803-ARE form and their receipt to the VA. 3 Start Networking and Join Professional Associations in Maine Networking is vital for business success. To connect with fellow home inspectors in Maine, consider joining the Maine Coalition of Home Inspection Professionals (MeCHIPs) and national bodies like the American Society of Home Inspectors (ASHI) and the International Association of Certified Home Inspectors (InterNACHI). Additionally, engaging with local real estate agents and businesses can help you establish valuable connections and grow your client base. 4 Secure General Liability and Errors and Omissions (E&O) Insurance Mistakes can happen, and having the proper insurance ensures you are financially protected against potential claims. General liability insurance typically costs about $40 per month, while errors and omissions (E&O) insurance averages $59 per month. Speak with a licensed insurance agent familiar with home inspection businesses, connect with industry peers, or explore online providers to find the best coverage for your needs. 5 Start Your Business or Join a Franchise Launching your home inspection career as part of a franchise can provide you with immediate brand recognition, training, and ongoing support. WIN Home Inspection, consistently ranked as the #1 home inspection franchise by Entrepreneur, offers comprehensive training and support without additional fees. By joining a franchise like WIN, you gain access to proven systems, marketing tools, and a community of professionals to help you quickly establish and grow your business.

section: 5 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Maryland
subsection: 
---

1 Complete an Approved Training Program 2 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam 3 Submit Your Application 4 Obtain Proof of Insurance 5 Receive Your License

1 Complete an Approved Training Program Applicants must complete a Commission-approved training program consisting of at least 72 hours of classroom-based instruction. This training equips candidates with foundational knowledge for their career and prepares them for the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE). A copy of the completion certificate must be submitted with the application. 2 Take and Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) The NHIE evaluates candidates on their knowledge of home inspection practices, covering topics such as Property and Building Inspection, Analysis of Findings, and Professional Responsibilities. The exam consists of 200 multiple-choice questions, with 4 hours allotted for completion. A scaled score of 500 or higher is required to pass. Each attempt costs approximately $225. Note: Veterans may qualify for reimbursement of the NHIE exam fee under the GI Bill. To utilize this benefit, submit the VBA-22-0803-ARE form along with your exam receipt to the VA. 3 Submit Your Application Applicants must submit a completed application to the Maryland Department of Labor. The application requires: Proof of a high school diploma or equivalent A certificate of completion for the approved training program NHIE score report A $50 application review fee 4 Obtain Proof of Insurance Maryland requires home inspectors to carry general liability insurance of at least $150,000. Proof of insurance must be submitted as part of the application process. 5 Receive Your License Once all requirements are met, the Department will issue your license, which is valid for a two-year term.

section: Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Mississippi
subsection: 
---

1 Complete a Mississippi-Approved Course 2 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam 3 Obtain General Liability Insurance 4 Acquire Errors and Omissions Insurance 5 Pay Application and Licensing Fees 6 Submit the Application

1 Complete a Mississippi-Approved 60-Hour Home Inspection Course The first step is completing a 60-hour training program approved by the Mississippi Home Inspector Board. This training will provide you with the skills and knowledge required for conducting home inspections. 2 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) After completing your education, you will need to take and pass the NHIE, a comprehensive exam consisting of 200 multiple-choice questions. The fee for the exam is approximately $225, and a score of 500 or higher is required for passing. 3 Obtain General Liability Insurance Mississippi home inspectors are required to carry general liability insurance with a minimum coverage amount of $250,000 to protect themselves from potential claims. 4 Acquire Errors and Omissions Insurance Inspectors must also have errors and omissions (E&O) insurance with a minimum coverage of $250,000 per occurrence. This policy protects inspectors from claims related to negligence or mistakes in their inspections. 5 Pay Application and Licensing Fees To apply for your license, you must submit a $175 application fee and a $325 licensing fee to the Mississippi Real Estate Commission’s Home Inspector Division. 6 Submit Application and Supporting Documents Along with your application, you must include a copy of your high school or college diploma/transcript, proof of insurance, and fingerprints for a background check. Ensure all forms are notarized before submission.

section: 5 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Nevada
subsection: 
---

1 Complete Pre-Licensing Education 2 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam 3 Gain Inspection Experience 4 Obtain Proof of Insurance 5 Submit Your Application and Pay the Fee

1 Complete Pre-Licensing Education Candidates must complete a board-approved training program. The required education hours vary depending on the license type: 40 hours for Residential Inspector 50 hours for General Inspector 60 hours for Master Inspector Applicants must submit a certificate of completion from their course along with their application. 2 Take and Pass the National Home Inspector Exam The NHIE consists of 200 multiple-choice questions across three domains and has a time limit of four hours. Each attempt costs approximately $225. Taking a prep course is recommended to improve your chances of passing on the first attempt. 3 Gain Inspection Experience To qualify, residential inspectors must complete 25 home inspections under the supervision of a certified general or master inspector. A certificate verifying the completion of these supervised inspections is required. 4 Obtain Proof of Insurance Home inspectors in Nevada must carry $100,000 in Errors and Omissions coverage and $100,000 in General Liability coverage. Ensure that your personal name is included in the insurance documents. 5 Submit Your Application and Pay the Fee All candidates, whether residents or non-residents, must be at least 18 years old and submit a complete application using Form 573 . The application fee is $365. Payment can be made by check or money order to the Nevada Real Estate Division, cash (exact change), or credit card for in-person transactions. Applicants must provide a fingerprint card along with a cashier’s check or money order payable to the Department of Public Safety. Alternatively, they can submit a verification form from an approved fingerprint vendor through Form 619 .

subsection:

1 Fulfill Educational Requirements 2 Complete 180 Hours of Licensing Training 3 Take and Pass the NHIE 4 Obtain Insurance Coverage 5 Submit Your Application

1 Fulfill Educational Requirements You must have a high school diploma or GED as a prerequisite to becoming a home inspector in New Jersey. 2 Complete 180 Hours of Licensing Training New Jersey requires 180 hours of home inspection education, which includes at least 40 hours of unpaid, field-based inspections supervised by a licensed home inspector. The training is provided by schools offering an approved course of study. 3 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) The NHIE consists of 200 multiple-choice questions covering three critical domains: Property and Building Inspection, Analysis of Findings and Reporting, and Professional Responsibilities. The exam fee is $225, and while you may retake the exam, you must wait 30 days between attempts and pay the exam fee for each attempt. 4 Obtain Insurance Coverage New Jersey home inspectors must have Errors and Omissions (E&O) insurance coverage with a minimum of $500,000 per occurrence. This ensures protection in case of liability or errors. 5 Submit Your Application Once all the requirements are met, submit your application, along with the $125 non-refundable application fee, to the New Jersey Home Inspector Licensing Board.

1 Complete a 120-Hour Pre-Licensing Course Candidates must complete a North Carolina-approved 120-hour pre-licensing course. This requirement, established by the North Carolina Home Inspection Licensure Act, covers business practices and essential inspection skills. 2 Complete 80 Hours of Field Training Applicants must complete an 80-hour field training course, which includes conducting 10 supervised site visits. This hands-on training provides practical experience and prepares candidates for real-world inspections. 3 Pass the North Carolina State Home Inspector Exam The state exam is administered at the North Carolina Department of Insurance in Raleigh multiple times a year. The exam fee is $80, and thorough preparation is recommended. 4 Undergo a Background Check Applicants must submit a criminal history record check through an approved provider, such as the North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation (SBI) or CastleBranch.com. 5 Obtain Insurance North Carolina requires home inspectors to have: A General Liability policy with at least $250,000 in coverage One of the following: Assets valued between $5,000 and $10,000 A surety bond between $5,000 and $10,000 An Errors & Omissions policy with at least $250,000 in coverage 6 Submit Your Application Complete the online application through the North Carolina Department of Insurance website. Include the $35 application fee. If your license is granted, a $160 licensing fee applies.

section: 6 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Ohio
subsection: 
---

1 Complete an 80-Hour Pre-Licensing Course 2 Fulfill Field Training Requirements 3 Pass the NHIE 4 Undergo a Background Check 5 Obtain Insurance 6 Submit Your Application

1 Complete an 80-Hour Pre-Licensing Course Applicants must take a state-approved 80-hour home inspection training course. This program is designed to prepare candidates for the National Home Inspector Exam and cover essential industry topics. 2 Fulfill Field Training Requirements Candidates must meet one of the following requirements: Complete 40 hours of supervised curriculum experience and undergo a peer review, or Conduct 10 parallel inspections under the supervision of a certified home inspector. 3 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) The NHIE evaluates candidates on their knowledge of home inspection practices, covering topics such as Property and Building Inspection, Analysis of Findings, and Professional Responsibilities. The exam consists of 200 multiple-choice questions, with 4 hours allotted for completion. A scaled score of 500 or higher is required to pass. Each attempt costs approximately $225. Note: Veterans may qualify for reimbursement of the NHIE exam fee under the GI Bill. To utilize this benefit, submit the VBA-22-0803-ARE form along with your exam receipt to the VA. 4 Undergo a Background Check Applicants must complete a background check, including fingerprinting, through the Bureau of Criminal Identification and Investigation (BCI&I). Arrange this through a Webcheck® user and present a government-issued photo ID. 5 Obtain Insurance Home inspectors in Ohio must carry: $100,000 in liability insurance per occurrence $300,000 aggregate coverage 6 Submit Your Application Complete the REPL-19-0003 Home Inspector License Application, have it notarized, and include: Supervisor’s signature (if applicable) Certificates of education and field training completion $250 application fee Lastly, submit your application to the Ohio Division of Real Estate & Professional Licensing.

section: 7 Steps to Become a Home Inspector in Pennsylvania
subsection: 
---

1 Take a Certified Training Course 2 Pass the NHIE 3 Obtain Insurance Coverage 4 Conduct 100 Paid, Supervised Inspections 5 Complete Your Education 6 Join a National Home Inspector Group 7 Start Your Business or Join a Franchise

1 Take a Certified Home Inspection Training Course Although Pennsylvania does not require licensing, obtaining professional training is essential. Enrolling in a reputable home inspection certification program provides foundational knowledge about inspection standards, business practices, and state-specific guidelines. Certification enhances your credibility and sets you apart in the competitive marketplace, making you a preferred choice for real estate agents, lenders, and homeowners. 2 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) While not mandatory in Pennsylvania, taking the NHIE establishes your expertise and builds trust with clients. The NHIE consists of 200 multiple-choice questions across three domains and has a time limit of four hours. Each attempt costs approximately $225. Taking a prep course is recommended to improve your chances of passing on the first attempt. Note: Veterans can have exam costs reimbursed through the GI Bill by submitting a VBA-22-0803-ARE form and their receipt to the VA. 3 Obtain Insurance Coverage Pennsylvania mandates specific insurance coverage for home inspectors: General Liability Insurance: At least $100,000 per occurrence. Errors & Omissions (E&O) Insurance: At least $100,000 per occurrence. Aggregate Coverage: $500,000 with a maximum deductible of $2,500. These policies protect your business and ensure compliance with state regulations. 4 Conduct 100 Paid, Supervised Inspections To gain experience and meet professional standards, complete 100 paid, supervised home inspections. This requirement helps you build confidence and prepares you for independent practice or working within a team. 5 Enroll and Complete the Required Education Program Home inspector training must be approved by the Texas Real Estate Commission (TREC). To obtain the Real Estate Inspector license, 154 hours of education (including 40 hours of practicum) are required, and to obtain the Professional Real Estate Inspector license, 194 hours of education are required (including 40 hours of practicum). 6 Join a National, Non-profit Home Inspection Association Membership in a national, non-profit home inspection association is required to operate in Pennsylvania. These associations provide training, resources, and a code of ethics. Popular options include: American Society of Home Inspectors (ASHI) International Association of Certified Home Inspectors (InterNACHI) 7 Start Your Business or Join a Franchise Consider joining a franchise like WIN Home Inspection to kickstart your career. Consistently ranked the #1 home inspection franchise by Entrepreneur, WIN offers comprehensive training, tools, and a recognized brand to help you succeed. WIN’s proprietary services, like the Healthy Home Check, ensure demand beyond the traditional real estate market.

1 Complete 40 Hours of State-Approved Education South Dakota requires applicants to complete a 40-hour state-approved home inspection course to meet the initial requirements for becoming a Registered Home Inspector. 2 Pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) Once your education is complete, you must pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE). subsection:

1 Fulfill Education Requirements 2 Pass the NHIE 3 Apply for a License 4 Obtain the Proper Insurance 5 Maintain Your License

1 Enroll and Complete the Required Education Program Home inspector training must be approved by the Texas Real Estate Commission (TREC). To obtain the Real Estate Inspector license, 154 hours of education (including 40 hours of practicum) are required, and to obtain the Professional Real Estate Inspector license, 194 hours of education are required (including 40 hours of practicum). 2 Pass the National Home Inspectors Exam (NHIE) In Texas, home inspectors must pass the National Home Inspector Exam (NHIE) and the state-specific exam. These exams can be taken throughout the year and proof of passing is required to apply for the home inspector license. These exams must be proctored. 3 Apply for a License To apply for a license, submit your application and all required documentation (including exam scores, proof of financial responsibility, and proof of completed education) to TREC. The application fee is $100 for the Real Estate Inspector license and $120 for the Professional Real Estate Inspector license. An additional $10 fee is applied after passing the exam. 4 Obtain the Proper Insurance Provide proof of Liability Insurance with a minimum of $100,000 per occurrence and an aggregate annual total of a minimum of $100,000 using the TREC Certificate of Insurance form or provide proof of a Surety Bond using the TREC Proof of Financial Responsibility Form. 5 Maintain Licensing Through Continuing Education Texas has specific continuing education (CE) requirements that all licensed home inspectors must complete on an annual and biannual basis. See below for the continuing education requirements.

1. What is the salary of home inspectors in Texas? Home inspectors in Texas can expect to make an average of $43,000 per year, up to $103,000 and at least $18,000 when you’re just starting out. 2. How long does it take to become a licensed home inspector in Texas? To obtain a Professional Real Estate Inspector license in Texas, it requires 194 hours of education.
